metadata.note: The Ithaca-Auburn Short Line -- the last railroad built in Tompkins County, and a famously ill-conceived one. Promoted by Albert H. Flint and chartered March 16 1900 as the New York, Auburn and Lansing Railroad, it revived the old 'Murdock Line' grade abandoned by the New York and Oswego Midland Railroad's Auburn Branch. Construction began in 1906 from the Auburn end and reached South Lansing March 1 1908; the line into Ithaca opened December 12 1908. The railroad was split by traction: roughly 29 miles of steam road ran Auburn - South Lansing, while the ~7 miles from South Lansing down into Ithaca were strung with overhead wire and worked by streetcars leased from the Ithaca Street Railway, using that company's Tioga Street line from downtown Ithaca out to Percy Field. Passengers between Ithaca and Auburn therefore had to change cars at South Lansing. The steam section offered four trains a day. A 0.5-mile electrified branch to the Rogues' Harbor Inn at South Lansing was added in 1909 (too short to draw at this scale; closed October 19 1920). The company went into receivership in 1912 and was reorganized as the Central New York Southern Railroad (organized May 28 1914, property conveyed July 14 1914), which bought McKeen motor cars so trains could run through without the transfer. It never worked: the route crossed very thinly settled country and paralleled the rapidly improving state Route 34. The last run over the main line was October 19 1923, the railroad was formally abandoned in 1924, and rail was lifted in 1925 -- except the Ithaca - Remington stretch, which the Ithaca Traction Corporation kept operating until 1931. Not to be confused with the earlier Ithaca, Auburn and Western Railroad (1876-1891), a different company over part of the same Murdock grade, whose Auburn end passed to the Lehigh Valley (see lehigh_valley_railroad.geojson). GEOMETRY IS A REAL-PLACE WAYPOINT APPROXIMATION following the documented route (Ithaca - Percy Field - Remington - South Lansing - North Lansing - Genoa - Venice - Scipio - Mapleton - Auburn), with straight-line segments between those points -- NOT digitized from period track maps or the surviving grade.

Flint, chartered March 16 1900; reused the Murdock Line grade of the NY&OM Auburn Branch; construction began 1906 from Auburn, reached South Lansing March 1 1908, opened into Ithaca December 12 1908; electric Ithaca - South Lansing using Ithaca Street Railway's Tioga Street line to Percy Field and leased streetcars, steam north of South Lansing with four daily trains; route via Genoa, Venice, Scipio, Mapleton to a Lehigh Valley connection at Auburn; 0.5-mile electrified Rogues' Harbor Inn branch built 1909, closed October 19 1920; receivership 1912, reorganized as Central New York Southern Railroad organized May 28 1914 / property conveyed July 14 1914; McKeen cars ended the transfer; last main-line run October 19 1923, formally abandoned 1924, rail removed 1925, Ithaca - Remington retained by Ithaca Traction Corporation until 1931)

http://www.swampstomper.nl/history/railways.html (D.G. Rossiter, Ithaca-area railway history: the line 'was a mistake from the beginning, running as it did through a very sparsely populated area', and the improving highway system, especially parallel state Route 34, caused the 1923 abandonment)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency of the electric Ithaca - South Lansing service (headway estimated); whether the four-daily-train steam schedule held through the Central New York Southern era; service levels on the Ithaca - Remington remnant 1923-1931; the surveyed alignment between Percy Field and South Lansing, which climbed out of the Ithaca valley by a route not captured here.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
